title: Derived Hom groups from a constructible integral complex commute with countable bounded-below sums
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]; noetherian means a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, and finite-dimensional means a finite bound on lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. Write $A_Y(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_Y(V)=C(|V|,E)$ on the small pro-etale site of any locally closed subscheme $Y$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $S_Y(M)=E_Y\otimes_{A_Y}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Constructible integral means continuous-constructible as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module], with local models $A_Y\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented $A$-modules $P$ on finitely many locally closed strata. Identify $A_X$ with the completed coefficient sheaf $\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] by the canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Let $D=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$ be the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and let $K$ belong, under this identification, to the bounded constructible complete category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For every small countable family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ in $D$ with a common cohomological lower bound and every integer $q$, the canonical map of $A$-modules
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_D(K,M_i[q])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_D\bigl(K,(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i)[q]\bigr)$$
is an isomorphism. The map is induced by the shifted coprojections. The empty family is allowed; no assertion about families without a common lower bound is made.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12; passage from global derived Hom to its cohomology, expanded using the shifted internal-Hom and K-injective interfaces.

proof.text: Use the coefficient-sheaf identification in the statement throughout. Put $B=\bigoplus_i M_i$ in $D$, write $\iota_i:M_i\to B$ for the coprojections, and set $G(N)=R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_X}(K,N)\in D(A)$ using the scalar-valued definition of global derived Hom. Apply the existing bounded-below compactness theorem with $T=X$, the same $E,A,\varpi,K$, and this family. Its scheme and constructibility hypotheses are exactly ours; the given common lower bound is sufficient, and a small countable family is in particular small. It gives an isomorphism $\alpha:\bigoplus_iG(M_i)\to G(B)$ whose composite with the $i$th coprojection is $G(\iota_i)$. This invokes the stronger, already existing derived-Hom theorem; no compactness assertion for unbounded-below families is used.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 (and Lemma 6.8.11(3) for the coefficient-category convention); existing common-lower-bound formulation.

proof.text: Apply $H^q:D(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ to $\alpha$. The derived-module cohomology-coproduct theorem, with $R=A$ and $E_i=G(M_i)$, identifies $H^q(\bigoplus_iG(M_i))$ with $\bigoplus_iH^qG(M_i)$ by the maps induced by its coprojections. It has no boundedness requirement on these $E_i$. Consequently the composite $\beta:\bigoplus_iH^qG(M_i)\to H^qG(B)$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules, and its $i$th component is $H^qG(\iota_i)$. This is valid for every integer $q$, including negative $q$, and for the empty family.

source.place: Tag 07D9, Lemma lemma-derived-products, clauses (1)-(2); termwise sums and exactness of module sums.

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site closed symmetric monoidal theorem to the small site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $\mathcal O=A_X$. Its tensor-Hom adjunction and symmetry make $H_K(N)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(K,N)$ a right adjoint of $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$, as required by the sections-model theorem. That theorem gives $\theta_N:H^qG(N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(K,N[q])$ for every $N$, naturally in $N$. To check coefficients, use the definition of $G$: its derived sections are computed on K-injective complexes of $A_X$-modules. Forgetting $A$ from their global-section complexes gives exactly the complexes defining abelian-group-valued derived sections in the model theorem. Kernels and images are unchanged on forgetting scalars, so the displayed cohomology identification applies to the underlying groups of $H^qG(N)$. Multiplication by $a\in A$ comes from the constant scalar section and is postcomposition by $a\,1_N$ on the model Hom complex. Naturality of the model identification for that endomorphism shows that $\theta_N$ is $A$-linear. Its stated naturality on K-injective target maps descends through localization and therefore applies to every derived coprojection $\iota_i$. No boundedness or flatness of $N$ is required.

source.place: Tags 08J7 and 08J9 (derived tensor-Hom adjunction), 08JA (global derived Hom), and 0A96 (K-flat/K-injective model); shifted Hom complex in every degree.

proof.text: Conjugate $\beta$ by $\bigoplus_i\theta_{M_i}$ and $\theta_B$. On the $i$th summand, naturality gives $u:K\to M_i[q]\mapsto\iota_i[q]\circ u:K\to B[q]$. The universal property of the module direct sum therefore identifies this conjugate with precisely the canonical map in the statement. Since all three maps used in the conjugation are isomorphisms, the required map is an isomorphism. For $I=\varnothing$, $B=0$ and both sides are zero, in agreement with the same argument.

lean.note: Uses the published PbcIntegralCategory specialization and its canonical ULift of the valuation ring. The ambient coproduct is an arbitrary colimiting cofan. DirectSum.toModule and Linear.rightComp give the actual coefficient-linear comparison induced by the shifted coprojections; bijectivity is precisely that this linear map is an isomorphism.
